causesCorrected: The keyboards looked wrong because of a BOX-MODEL hole, not a styling drift: the properties that centre a key's glyph live on `button, .button`, which a <span class="key"> does not match, so letters sat top-left at the wrong weight.

The parity values had to come from tui-shell.css, not globals.css - tui-shell redeclares `button, .button` and loads second, so a real key computes font-weight 650 and letter-spacing 0, not 700 and 0.015em. Copying the first rule found would have made every figure key bolder than the keyboard it imitates.

Both keyboards showed one accent because the data-accent attributes DID NOTHING: the accent blocks were still scoped to :root, which is <html>, so an attribute on a nested div matched no selector. Planned in v7.3 and never executed in the port; the approved artifact had relaxed selectors, which is why it looked right there and wrong in the app.

The game has NO pressed state at all: globals.css sets button:active { translate: 0 1px } and tui-shell.css cancels it with translate: 0. The only visible key state is the hover treatment, which on touch IS the tap state.
SUBMIT and DELETE were missing, so the figure's row three had seven keys where the real one has nine - making its letters WIDER than row one when the real ones are narrower.

The v10 report found that pattern and dismissed it on the strength of a check reporting 'no triggers on async_multiplayer_games'. There are two. That check was wrong and it cost the investigation its best lead. v10_3DailyStreak.design: one optional field, lastDailyDate, on the durable progress record. Optional is load-bearing: progressSchema is strict and pinned to schemaVersion 1, so a required field would reject every record written before it existed - the same way appliedRewards and dailyEntitlements were added. New domain module src/domain/daily-streak.ts holds localDayKey, previousDayKey, advanceDailyStreak, currentDailyStreak and streakDateForEntry, all pure, with today passed in rather than read
v10_3DailyStreak.idempotencyByDate: keyed on the day rather than on an operation id, deliberately. That is the same property that makes finishing both the OG and the GO on one day count once and makes a retried finalize a no-op. An operation id would have counted the second mode as a second day
v10_3DailyStreak.noMigrationReason: the record is JSON inside a game_history sentinel row, so a new field is not a schema change. The one place SQL touches it is the account reset (20260802193000_amordle_account_lifecycle_v1.sql:280-300), which zeroes dailyStreak and cannot know about a field added later. Rather than a forward migration, the transform reads a stored streak of 0 as 'no streak' and restarts at 1 whatever date is on record. This is why two fields beat a set of recent dates: a set survives the reset and would resurrect a streak the owner had just cleared, and THAT would need a migration
v10_3DailyStreak.xpGateDefectAvoided: the XP write was gated on rewardXp > 0, and a Daily loss with nothing solved earns no XP - exactly the case the owner asked to count. Hanging the streak off that gate would have shipped a streak that silently ignored every bad day. The two now share one writeAccountProgressCas call: one round trip, one revision bump, and a no-op stays a no-op
v10_3DailyStreak.displayLapses: a stored streak is only current while lastDailyDate is today or yesterday, so the panel cannot show a stale 7 to somebody who stopped a month ago. The apply rule restarts at 1 after a gap, so store and display can never disagree. Zero reads 'start today' when no Daily was ever finished and 'start again' when one was
v10_3DailyStreak.duplicateDayKey: the local day key existed twice, copy-pasted between calendar-view.tsx and daily-access-gate.tsx. Both now import one function. Neither changed WHEN it runs - both still defer behind queueMicrotask, because computing the local day during SSR bakes in the server's day
v10_3DailyStreak.endToEndProof: the suite had never played a Daily; it seeded one through the legacy import and asserted the panel, leaving play -> outbox -> finalize -> CAS -> record -> panel unproven against a deployment. services.combat.spec.ts now plays today's OG Daily TO A LOSS on the deployed build: nothing solved earns no XP and no coins, so it is precisely the case the old gate would have skipped, and the run asserts the balances are untouched while the streak still moves. The account's imported streak is dated 2026-07-20, so it also proves lapse-then-restart rather than an increment. Recorded: result lost, rewardedXp 0, rewardedCoins 0, streakAfter 1, lapsedFrom 2026-07-20, lastDailyDate 2026-08-15. Guesses are drawn from outside the answer catalog, so the game cannot be won by accident and the test never has to agree with the server about which word today holds
v10_3DailyStreak.gateAsDomainRule: streakDateForEntry is a named domain rule compared by test against rows buildSoloHistoryRow actually produces, not a restated copy. kind === 'solo-daily' rather than lane === 'daily', because V1 entries carry no lane and the COMBAT Daily is UTC-keyed and must never feed a local-day streak. hostingCostAssessment.firstPaidTier: Supabase Pro $25/mo (8 GB db, 250 GB egress then $0.09/GB, 100k MAU, 500 realtime connections, 5M messages, 7-day backups, never paused) - 50x the egress ceiling, moving the wall from ~200 players to ~10,000. Vercel Pro $20/user/mo (1 TB, 10M edge requests) is not needed for capacity; it would be needed only if the project stopped being non-commercial, or for spend management so an overage bills instead of pausing. MOST LIKELY reason to ever pay is the free project pausing after a quiet week, not scale
hostingCostAssessment.expensiveFasterThanNecessary: 1. NotificationCenter polls 4 endpoints every 30 s on every page forever - the single largest line item, paid by players reading the Help page. 120 s cuts it 4x; collapsing to one RPC cuts it again. 2. It ALSO holds three UNFILTERED postgres_changes subscriptions (notification-center.tsx:145-160), each event triggering a full 4-call refetch - but the async_multiplayer_games read policy admits only authority_version = 0 rows, so realtime should deliver nothing for v2 games. Both mechanisms paid for, one delivered. UNVERIFIED against a live match - worth watching whether it ever fires. 3. listLegacyRecent queries authority_version = 0 every 30 s per player forever - a compatibility query on an endless schedule. 4. The 5 s polls stack: active-games + match-controller + portal + notifications is ~30 req/min from one player watching one game
hostingCostAssessment.whatToMeasure: Three numbers replace every estimate. (a) Bytes per notification-feed cycle: DevTools Network filtered to the Supabase host, signed in, sitting on /combat for two minutes, transferred total / 2 = MB/min. This turns the 150-500 player range into a figure. (b) Vercel Active CPU and Edge Requests month-to-date, dashboard Usage. (c) Supabase egress and database size month-to-date, dashboard Reports Usage
hostingCostAssessment.uncertainty: Every REQUEST RATE in the report is read out of the source and is exact. Every BYTE figure is an estimate and is labelled as one. The 2 KB mean response assumption is the load-bearing guess and is the first thing to measure
hostingCostAssessment.CORRECTED_2026_08_18: MEASURED, and the earlier figure is superseded. The assessment estimated 150-500 regular players before Supabase free-tier egress binds, from FOUR requests per 30s cycle at an assumed 2 KB per response. Both inputs were wrong and they CANCELLED: the cycle was four to twenty-four requests, responses are ~1.1 KB raw and ~0.2 KB compressed rather than 2 KB, and response headers were ignored entirely - they are 84% of the old path's cost. Measured per signed-in tab-hour: 0.578 MB before v10.6, 0.049 MB after. Players at 30 min/day: 590 before, 7014 after. At 60 min/day: 295 before, 3507 after. So the published range was SLIGHTLY PESSIMISTIC rather than understated, which is the opposite of what I predicted - it is understated only for a player with a long Practice history, where the rematch fan-out drops the old path to 109-280 players. EGRESS IS NO LONGER THE BINDING CONSTRAINT: the next wall is 200 concurrent realtime connections, then the 500 MB database
hostingCostAssessment.loadBearingAssumption: that response HEADERS count toward Supabase egress metering. They are 84% of the old path's cost and they do traverse the wire, but the accounting is inferred rather than read. If headers are excluded, the v10.6 saving is 4.1x rather than 11.9x - because collapsing four calls into one saved almost NO payload; the new response is larger raw and 23 bytes smaller gzipped. The entire benefit is fewer round trips and a slower rate

reportDeliveryPolicy.rule: EVERY canonical report gets a published Claude Artifact companion, and the link is handed to the owner in the same message that announces the work. A Markdown report on a phone is an unrendered wall of terminal text or a file that has to be fetched before it can be read. Work that is finished but unreadable at the moment of review is not finished from his side
reportDeliveryPolicy.appliesTo: cycle and release reports, migration decision packets, assessments and plans, incident write-ups, and any handoff where the owner is expected to review, decide or approve. reportDeliveryPolicy.artifactMust: 1. LEAD WITH ANYTHING LIVE - an outstanding deploy, Production mismatched with its database, a player-visible fault - before the narrative and styled so it cannot be scrolled past. 2. State what the owner must run, in order, with a copy control that still works when the clipboard API is blocked. 4.
